preamble: Delateralization of the palatalized lateral [lʲ] to the palatal glide [j]: the lateral gesture is lost and the secondary palatal articulation remains as the whole consonant. This is documented in the Carpatho-Rusyn dialect of Komlóska (Komloška), north-eastern Hungary, where palatalized ľ of every Proto-Slavic source (*ľ, *lj, *lь, *lě, *lę) became j in all positions: aprij 'April', jubyty 'to love', chjib 'bread', ned'ija 'Sunday'. The Camuno plural example formerly filed here (gal ~ gaj) is a morphological alternation from a Latin -LLI palatal lateral stage and has been removed.

examples.note: Palatalized lateral after a consonant > j.

sources: Benedek, G. (2007). Судьба палатализованного л' в русинском говоре села Комлошка [The fate of palatalized l' in the Rusyn dialect of Komlóska]. Studia Slavica, 52(1–2), 39–42. https://doi.org/10.1556/SSlav.52.2007.1-2.6
